authorization: Protocols only. This proposer run does not train, submit jobs, download data, or edit existing files.

experiments.question: Can the kept temporal farm checkpoint reproduce large departures in its own 1979-2017 training years?
inputs: the unchanged event thresholds already documented: absolute valley temperature departure greater than 2 K or absolute valley precipitation departure greater than 10 mm
protocol: Run inference only with the kept epoch-26 checkpoint; do not optimize.
Select all 1979-2017 event weeks using targets, then score both event and matched quiet weeks.

For each channel record observed and model valley departure, sign, model_valley_departure_rms / observed_valley_departure_rms, physical RMSE, season, magnitude bin, and whether the last-14-day departure has the same sign.
Report medians and hit fractions by temperature/rain, magnitude bin, and precursor class. A hit has the observed sign and at least half the observed departure, matching the existing event definition.
Compare with 2018 and 2019 using the same table. Do not tune thresholds on 2019.

discriminator.capacity_loss_architecture: Large training events are also shrunken or wrong-sign.
discriminator.predictability_generalization: Training events are fit in-sample but analogous 2018-2019 events collapse.
discriminator.sample_scarcity: Fit quality degrades strongly in sparsely populated season-sign-magnitude bins.

experiments.pass_or_stop: This is a diagnostic, not a model gate. If training extremes are underfit, test path/loss before claiming a predictability limit. If they are fit but held-out extremes fail, do not expect loss reweighting alone to solve generalization.

experiments.question: How strongly does the temporal farm shrink departures already present in scored files?
protocol: Use score_example fields already present: model_valley_departure_rms, observed_valley_departure_rms, and their ratio.
Sort by observed departure magnitude and compare ratios for already_in_condition, inside_first_week, reversal, after_day_7, and quiet labels.
Read temperature and precipitation separately; do not average physical units.
Flag wrong-direction cases where a large observed departure has a model departure of the opposite sign.
experiments.falsifier: If ratios approach one on large, already-in-condition 2018-2019 events and signs are correct, broad conditional-mean collapse is not supported.

experiments.question: Is the precursor lost at temporal pooling or later in the spatial/output path?
protocol: Save last_day_weights for valley, Gulf, and upstream patches.
Repeat inference after replacing days 1-76 by their training-date mean, then after replacing days 77-90; do not optimize.
Repeat with only root-zone soil or precipitation on days 77-90 perturbed to its reference-state value.
Measure changes in valley departure, not only attention weights.

discriminator.temporal_pooling: Recent precursor removal changes the relevant patch token but the learned attention had diluted it.
discriminator.spatial_or_decoder: The patch summary responds to the precursor but the valley output does not.
discriminator.missing_predictor: Neither patch summaries nor output responds and no stored-field perturbation separates events.

experiments.falsifier: The relevant recent days dominate weights and perturbations propagate to a correct valley departure; temporal pooling is then not the bottleneck.

experiments.explicit_delta_from_blocked_runs: Convex 0.3 global / 0.7 two-channel valley objective on the 1,976-week TemporalSpatialReslim farm. Prior det_v2_reslim_valley added valley temperature weight 1 on the older 145-file Reslim; det_v2_reslim_valley01 added 0.1 of each valley channel while retaining full global weight.
fixed_components: TemporalSpatialReslim patch 6, embed 64, depth 4, four heads, keep ratio 0.25
same 24 fields and per-channel training normalization
same optimizer, learning rate, clipping, and patience as temporal_reslim_farm
experiments.magnitude_note: The components must be logged separately. Existing metrics do not record an exact decomposition. The global-only farm is 0.823 train and 0.977 validation at kept epoch 26. On the older 145-file Reslim, global plus valley-T weight 1 is 3.280 train and 2.920 validation at kept epoch 2, while global plus 0.1*(valley-T+valley-P) is 0.885 train and 1.271 validation at kept epoch 28. These are different runs and cannot be subtracted to invent component MSEs; they show that a valley term is not numerically negligible.
experiments.epoch_rule: Keep the checkpoint with the lowest mean physical 2018 valley temperature RMSE across all 56 validation weeks, exactly matching the farm selector; break ties by the 2018 composite objective. Do not select on four 2018 dates, April rain, or any 2019 value.
required_logging: 2018 physical valley temperature and precipitation RMSE
pass: 2019 four-issue valley temperature mean at or under 0.7668 K
no 2019 issue week worse than det_v2_soil_k9: 0.5969, 0.8282, 1.2597, and 0.3825 K for January, April, July, and October
16-22 April 2019 valley rain at least 40.2 mm, against 55.9 mm observed, 24.4 mm climate, 24.7 mm 9x9, and 20.9 mm temporal farm
experiments.kill: Stop loss-only variants if either the temperature rule or April-rain rule fails. A better April temperature alone is insufficient: det_v2_reslim_valley already reached 0.710 K in April but its four-week mean was 0.916 K.
experiments.expected_result: Some valley movement, probably at the cost of the globe and with inconsistent issue-week effects. The 6-degree path bottleneck makes a full pass unlikely.

experiments.explicit_delta_from_prior: GEFS is a causal predictor, not a target to mimic and not a post-hoc replacement forecast. The model predicts ERA5 residuals using fixed issue-time ensemble statistics.
experiments.training_rows: Use only issue dates with GEFSv12 reforecast and HEADWATER examples in 2000-2017. Keep 2018 for epoch selection and 2019 for one final score. Do not fabricate GEFS for 1979-1999.
forecast_features: five-member ensemble-mean week-mean 2 m temperature anomaly relative to reference_train temperature
five-member ensemble standard deviation of week-mean 2 m temperature
five-member ensemble-mean seven-day precipitation anomaly relative to reference_train precipitation
five-member ensemble standard deviation of seven-day precipitation
bias_and_scaling: Compute all feature normalization from 2000-2017 only.
For temperature, either provide the raw ensemble anomaly plus a train-only calendar-date bias channel, or subtract a calendar-date bias fit on 2000-2017. Never fit an offset on 2018 or 2019.

The existing train-only offsets are +1.52 K January, +3.37 K April, +1.55 K July, and +2.33 K October; corrected 2019 GEFS still scores 1.047 K, so GEFS temperature must remain an input rather than a replacement.
Do not select the wettest member using the observed target. Mean and spread are available at issue time; hindsight member choice leaks.
experiments.injection: Add a gated 1-degree residual branch over the four GEFS fields, with the forecast valid-time maps regridded to the HEADWATER 1-degree grid. Fuse its two-channel correction after the 6-degree week head and alongside the existing local residual. The branch must not rely solely on 6-degree patch tokens. For the minimal isolation test, initialize from the kept temporal farm checkpoint, freeze the temporal-spatial trunk, and fit only the small GEFS branch on 2000-2017.

missing_year_policy.recommended_minimal: Train the GEFS branch only on 2000-2017 and keep the pre-2000 farm data only in the already-trained frozen trunk.
missing_year_policy.alternative_joint_model: Zero-fill forecast fields for 1979-1999, add an explicit availability mask, and multiply the GEFS branch output by that mask. This preserves old rows for trunk gradients but gives the branch no fake pre-2000 signal.
missing_year_policy.warning: A mask is perfectly confounded with era; do not interpret it as a climate predictor.

experiments.operational_note: The retrospective archive is GEFSv12 from 2000. Operational data from 2020 onward must be checked for version and field-contract continuity; the early part of 2020 should not be assumed to be operational v12. Score any 2020+ operational period as a distribution-shift test, not as extra training or epoch-selection data.
leakage_controls: Use only the 00 UTC issue forecast and hours available then: temperature at 24-168 h and precipitation accumulations ending by 168 h.
Fit regridding, bias correction, and normalization without 2018-2019 targets.
Do not use analyses from the target window, observed-member ranking, or a forecast initialized after the issue time.
Preserve chronological split and score 2019 once.
experiments.data_cost: scripts/score_gefs_reforecast.py performs index-guided byte-range fetches from noaa-gefs-retrospective and caches only retained messages. The current charge records 75 mornings at roughly 5 MB per member per variable; extending to every weekly farm date would be a materially larger new data build. The minimal experiment therefore stays on the four calendar issue dates and reuses the cache contract.
experiments.epoch_rule: Among branch checkpoints, keep the lowest mean 2018 four-issue valley temperature RMSE; break ties by April 2018 rain error, all specified before reading 2019.
pass: 2019 four-issue valley temperature mean at or under 0.7668 K
no issue week worse than the 9x9 values 0.5969, 0.8282, 1.2597, and 0.3825 K
16-22 April 2019 valley rain at least 40.2 mm
experiments.kill: If April rain remains below 40.2 mm or the temperature gate fails, do not enlarge the branch or fetch weekly GEFS farm inputs. First score days 8-14 without training; extend the forecast-input horizon only if those leads beat their date-specific climate.
experiments.expected_result: Rain should move for days 1-7 because the issue-time ensemble already moves April from 24.4 mm climate to 38.4 mm mean with a 23.3-49.3 mm spread. Temperature benefit is less certain because all eight scored raw forecasts are cold and the train-only offset does not clear the existing gate.

experiments.question: Does issue-time dynamical information remain useful in days 8-14?
protocol: Use the same eight 2018-2019 mornings, five members, valley cells, and latitude weights.
Score days 8-10 from the existing Days:1-10 object and fetch the documented next span for days 11-14.
Compare member mean and spread with ERA5 and the 1979-2017 climate of days 8-14. Do not fit a network.
experiments.decision: If days 8-14 sit near or behind climate, stop GEFS input at day 7. If they consistently beat climate on 2018 and 2019, define a separate lead-specific input and gate before any train.
